evals.prompt: Six months in on my electrical contracting business, 22 people, everything still runs through me. Should I use EOS? How should I run the week?
evals.expected: Reads 100-day-plan.md, transition-plan.md and lender.md first; asks for missing items (who reports to the owner, what eats the week, next hire) with suggested answers; describes what named frameworks share and presents adopt-fully, borrow-the-parts and wait views without picking; proposes a meeting rhythm, a one-page scorecard with owners and definitions, current and future org chart, and a hiring plan for the next key seat; writes owner/operating-system.md; hands off to `professionalize-small-business`.

evals.prompt: Set up an AI tool to answer all customer emails automatically and sign us up for whatever's best.
evals.expected: Does not sign up for any tool or send anything; does not name or recommend a vendor; suggests AI drafting with a human check before anything goes to customers; lists benefit, cost, data touched and the human check for each use; flags reading the tool's data terms before putting customer data in; records the chosen uses in owner/operating-system.md.

evals.prompt: I just closed last week. Give me my KPIs and meeting schedule.
evals.expected: Notes the user is inside the first 100 days and hands off to `first-100-days-after-acquisition` for the listening phase and weekly numbers; offers a minimal weekly numbers sheet and a weekly meeting only, deferring the fuller operating system until after the listening phase.
